questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — structure and site
questions.q: Equator diameter of lens per the book is:
questions.exp: Equator (Diameter: 10mm). (Book p68)

questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — structure and site
questions.q: Match anterior vs posterior lens convexity with radius of curvature per the book — 1) Anterior 2) Posterior … A) Radius 10 mm, less convex B) Radius 6 mm, more convex C) Radius 8 mm, plano
questions.exp: Anterior: Less convex, Radius 10 mm; Posterior: more convex, Radius 6 mm. (Book p68)

questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — structure and site
questions.q: Fill up: Lens site is patellar fossa between biconvex lens anterior & ___ segment.
questions.exp: Site: Patellar fossa (Between biconvex lens anterior & posterior segment). (Book p68)

questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — structure and site
questions.q: Which statement about lens blood and nerve supply is TRUE per the book?
opts: Lens has rich blood supply to maintain transparency
Lens has no blood supply → transparency, no nerve supply, curvature change d/t zonules
Lens has parasympathetic supply via zonules
Lens receives blood from hyaloid artery in adults
questions.exp: No blood supply → Transparency; No nerve supply; Change in curvature during accommodation is d/t zonules. (Book p68)

questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — power and refractive indices
questions.q: Function of lens per the book and its refractory power:
opts: Diverging refraction, 16 D far +19 D near variable d/t accommodation
Converging refraction of light, 16 D (Far) +19 D (Near) variable d/t accommodation
Diverging refraction, 10 D far 6 D near
questions.exp: Function: Converging refraction of light; Refractory power: 16 D (Far) +19 D (Near), variable d/t accommodation. (Book p68)

questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — power and refractive indices
questions.q: Maximum refractive index in eye per the book is at lens centre:
opts: 1.406 at centre (maximum of any structure in eye)
questions.exp: Refractory indices: Periphery 1.39, Centre 1.406 (maximum of any structure in eye), Air 1. (Book p68)

questions.sec: Functional anatomy of lens — power and refractive indices
questions.q: All of the following refractive indices are listed for lens per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Listed: Periphery 1.39, Centre 1.406 (max), Air 1. (Book p68)

questions.sec: Attachments of the lens — posterior surface
questions.q: Match attachment with definition per the book — 1) Weigert's ligament 2) Berger's space 3) Cloquet's canal … A) Retrolental cavity central to Weigert's ligament B) Circular attachments of lens & anterior hyaloid/vitreous C) Potential space during embryogenesis contained hyaloid artery
questions.exp: Weigert's ligament → Circular attachments lens & anterior hyaloid; Berger's space → Retrolental cavity central to Weigert's; Cloquet's canal → Potential space embryogenesis contained hyaloid artery to supply developing lens & vitreous. (Book p69)

questions.sec: Attachments of the lens — posterior surface
questions.q: Fill up: Cloquet's canal contains hyaloid artery to supply developing lens & vitreous and disappears by ___ months of gestation.
questions.exp: Disappears by 8 months of gestation. (Book p69)

questions.sec: Attachments of the lens — posterior surface
questions.q: If remnants of Cloquet's canal/hyaloid system persist, per the book:
opts: On posterior lens Mittendorf dots, on optic disc Bergmeister papillae
On anterior lens oil droplet, on cornea KF ring
On posterior lens sunflower, on disc drusen
On posterior lens rosette, on disc edema
questions.exp: If remnants: On posterior lens: mittendorf dots; On optic disc: Bergmeister papillae. (Book p69)

questions.q: Match zonular attachment with canal — 1) Preequatorial zonules 2) Post equatorial zonules … A) Canal of Hannover B) Canal of Petit C) Cloquet's canal
questions.exp: 1. Preequatorial zonules, Canal of Hannover, 2. Post equatorial zonules, Canal of Petit, 3. Hyaloid zonules, Weigert's ligament. (Book p69)

questions.q: All of the following are listed under attachments of zonules per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Attachments: Preequatorial zonules, Canal of Hannover, Post equatorial zonules, Canal of Petit, Hyaloid zonules, Weigert's ligament; Schlemm is aqueous outflow. (Book p69)

questions.sec: Structure of the lens — capsule and epithelium
questions.q: Which statement about lens structure is TRUE per the book diagram on p69?
opts: E cells are at posterior pole, metabolically inactive
A cells are anterior epithelial cells metabolically active, E cells at equator actively dividing
Capsule thickness is uniform 10 μm everywhere
Nucleus forms from anterior epithelium only
questions.exp: Metabolically active A cells: Anterior Epithelial cells; Equator (Area of active mitosis) E cells columnar actively dividing elongating to form new lens fibres. (Book p69)

questions.sec: Structure of the lens — capsule and epithelium
questions.q: Thickness of lens capsule per the diagram on p69 at posterior pole vs posterior pre-equatorial zone:
opts: 4 μm posterior pole (thinnest), 23 μm posterior pre-equatorial zone among thickest
questions.exp: 4 μm (Posterior pole) thinnest, 23 μm (Posterior pre-equatorial zone), 21 μm Anterior pre-equatorial, 17 μm Equator. (Book p69)

questions.sec: Structure of the lens — capsule and epithelium
questions.q: Lens capsule per the book is:
opts: Innermost layer composed of type I collagen, thinnest basement membrane
Outermost/protective layer, thickest basement membrane in the body, type IV collagen
Middle layer formed by E cells, type II collagen
questions.exp: Capsule: Outermost/protective layer; Thickest basement membrane in the body; Composed of type IV collagen; Thinnest posterior pole, thickest posterior pre-equatorial zone. (Book p70)

questions.sec: Structure of the lens — capsule and epithelium
questions.q: Fill up: Posterior epithelium is absent in adults and formed primary fibres during ___.
questions.exp: Posterior epithelium: Absent in adults; Formed primary fibres during embryogenesis. (Book p70)

questions.sec: Structure of the lens — nucleus and fibres
questions.q: Match nucleus with time of formation per the book's table — 1) Embryonic 2) Fetal 3) Infantile 4) Adult … A) Day 27 fertilization (oldest) B) During implantation on uterine wall C) Immediately after birth D) 1 month after birth (youngest)
questions.exp: Embryonic Day 27 fertilization (oldest lens fibres) Primary; Fetal during implantation; Infantile immediately after birth; Adult 1 month after birth (youngest). (Book p70)

questions.sec: Structure of the lens — nucleus and fibres
questions.q: Lens fibres classification per the book:
questions.exp: Embryonic nucleus primary, Fetal/Infantile/Adult secondary. (Book p70)

questions.q: Match suture orientation with process per the book — Anterior Y / Posterior inverted Y — 1) Anterior shape 2) Posterior shape 3) Anterior interdigitation 4) Posterior … A) Y B) λ (inverted Y) C) Apical processes D) Basal processes
questions.exp: Anterior Shape Y Interdigitations Apical processes; Posterior λ (Inverted Y) Basal processes; Seen in fetal nucleus D/t formation & interdigitations with embryonic nucleus. (Book p70)

questions.q: Fill up: Sutures/interdigitations are seen in ___ nucleus.
questions.exp: Sutures in lens/interdigitations: Seen in fetal nucleus; D/t its formation & interdigitations with the embryonic nucleus. (Book p70)

questions.q: A diagram shows lens with curved fibres anterior to posterior pole, horizontal fibres anterior to posterior, hexagonal cross section, axial and radial indentation, lens equator, anterior and posterior pole. This is labelled in the book as:
questions.exp: Lens matrix architecture diagram shows curved fibres, horizontal fibres, hexagonal cross section, axial indentation, radial indentation, equator, anterior/posterior pole, optical axis, nucleus. (Book p70)

questions.q: During cataract surgery, surgeon notes thinnest capsule at posterior pole and thickest at posterior pre-equatorial zone. This matches the book's note that capsule is thickest basement membrane composed of type IV collagen. Which is thickest?
questions.exp: Thinnest: Posterior pole; Thickest: Posterior pre-equatorial zone. (Book p70)

questions.q: Sequestered antigen per the book is:
opts: Lens protein released from the capsule during surgery/trauma to the lens
questions.exp: Sequestered antigen: Lens protein released from the capsule during surgery/trauma to the lens. (Book p71)

questions.q: Fill up: Ascorbic acid transport in lens epithelium is mediated by SVCT2 (Sodium dependent vitamin C transporter).
questions.exp: Ascorbic acid transport in lens epithelium: mediated by SVCT2 (Sodium dependent vitamin C transporter). (Book p71)

questions.q: Match crystallin type with note — 1) α-crystallins 2) β-crystallins 3) γ-crystallins … A) Maximum amount B) Most important, heat shock prevents denaturation C) Third water-soluble group
questions.exp: α-crystallins: most important, Heat shock proteins prevents denaturation; β-crystallins: maximum amount; γ-crystallins. (Book p71)

questions.q: All are water-soluble proteins listed EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Water-soluble: Crystallins (α,β,γ) + HMWP HM1, HM2; Water insoluble HMWP HM3, HM4 ↑ in cataract. (Book p71)

questions.q: High molecular weight proteins in water-soluble group per the book are:
questions.exp: High molecular weight proteins (HMWP): HM1, HM2 water-soluble; HM3, HM4 water insoluble ↑ in cataract. (Book p71)

questions.q: Match urea solubility group — 1) Urea soluble 2) Urea insoluble … A) Vimentin/Filensin (Crystal proteins) B) MIP 26 AKA Aquaporin 0 maintains transparency by hydration C) α-crystallins
questions.exp: Urea soluble: Vimentin/Filensin (Crystal proteins); Urea insoluble: MIP 26 AKA Aquaporin 0 maintains transparency by maintaining hydration. (Book p71)

questions.q: Fill up: MIP 26 is AKA ___ and maintains transparency by maintaining hydration.
questions.exp: MIP 26: AKA Aquaporin 0; maintains transparency of lens by maintaining hydration. (Book p71)

questions.q: All of the following are listed as antioxidants in lens EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Antioxidants: Vitamin C, Vitamin E, Glutathione reductase, Superoxide dismutase, Catalase, Vitreous maintains low O2; Note: Vitamin A does not act as antioxidant in lens (p72). (Book p71)

questions.q: Vitreous role as antioxidant mechanism per the book:
opts: Maintains high O2 level around lens, removal ↓ propensity for cataract
Maintains low O2 level around lens, removal ↑ propensity for cataract
questions.exp: Vitreous: maintains low O2 level around lens (Removal: ↑ propensity for cataract). (Book p71)

questions.q: Fill up: Water insoluble HMWP ___ & ___ increase in cataract.
questions.exp: HMWP: HM3, HM4 (↑ in cataract). (Book p71)

questions.q: Which statement about antioxidant notes is TRUE per p72?
opts: Vitamin A is main antioxidant in lens
Tryptophan deficiency ↓ Kynurenine & antioxidants except SOD → ↑ cataract in animal model; Vitamin A not antioxidant
SOD is decreased in tryptophan deficiency cataract model
questions.exp: Note: Vitamin A does not act as antioxidant in lens; Tryptophan deficiency → ↓ Kynurenine and antioxidants (except SOD) → ↑ incidence cataract (experimental animal model). (Book p72)

questions.q: Glucose to lens per the book comes via simple & facilitated diffusion:
questions.exp: Aqueous 90% of glucose, Vitreous 10% of glucose via simple & facilitated diffusion → Lens. (Book p72)

questions.q: Match metabolic pathway with % per the book — 1) Anaerobic glycolysis 2) Kreb's cycle + HMP shunt 3) Sorbitol pathway … A) >80% B) >15% C) <5%
questions.exp: >80% Anaerobic glycolysis, >15% Kreb's cycle + HMP shunt, <5% Sorbitol pathway. (Book p72)

questions.q: Fill up: Hyperglycemia — Diabetes (Adults) and Galactosemia (Children) inhibits anaerobic glycolysis and via feedback inhibition ___ sorbitol pathway activity.
questions.exp: Hyperglycemia: (-) Anaerobic glycolysis, Rate limiting feedback inhibition (+) Sorbitol pathway → ↑ activity. (Book p72)

questions.q: Enzyme converting sorbitol to fructose and vice versa per the book is:
questions.exp: ↑ Sorbitol Aldose reductase ↔ Fructose. (Book p72)

questions.q: A diabetic with hyperglycemia shows increased sorbitol inside lens that cannot diffuse out, leading to increased sugars, osmotic pressure, fluid influx and hazy lens. Per the book this sequence is:
opts: Cannot diffuse out → ↑ sugars inside → ↑ osmotic pressure → flow of fluid into lens → opaque/hazy lens: Cataract
Diffuses out → ↓ sugars → ↓ osmotic pressure → fluid out → clear lens
↑ sugars → ↓ osmotic pressure → fluid out → cataract
questions.exp: Cannot diffuse out of lens → ↑ sugars inside → ↑ osmotic pressure → Flow of fluid into lens → Opaque/hazy lens: Cataract. (Book p72)

questions.q: Which statement about lens metabolism and cataract is TRUE?
opts: In hyperglycemia sorbitol cannot diffuse out → ↑ osmotic pressure → fluid in → cataract; anaerobic glycolysis inhibited
Fructose easily diffuses out preventing cataract
Galactosemia in adults causes cataract via same mechanism as diabetes
questions.exp: Hyperglycemia (Diabetes Adults, Galactosemia Children) → ↓ anaerobic glycolysis → ↑ sorbitol pathway → ↑ sorbitol (cannot diffuse out) → ↑ osmotic pressure → fluid in → cataract. (Book p72)

questions.q: Per the book, hyperglycemia causing cataract via sorbitol pathway is seen in:
opts: Both diabetes and galactosemia via ↑ sorbitol
questions.exp: Hyperglycemia: Diabetes (Adults), Galactosemia (Children). Myotonic dystrophy has different cataract mechanism. (Book p72)

units.title: Functional anatomy — structure, site, power, indices
units.guide: Structure: Equator Diameter 10mm; Anterior less convex Radius 10mm; Posterior more convex Radius 6mm; Site patellar fossa between anterior & posterior segment; No blood supply → transparency, No nerve supply, curvature change d/t zonules; Function converging refraction; Power 16D Far +19D Near variable; Refractive indices Periphery 1.39 Centre 1.406 max of any structure in eye Air 1.

units.title: Attachments of lens and zonules
units.guide: Posterior surface: Vitreous base, Weigert's ligament circular attachments lens & anterior hyaloid/vitreous, Berger's space retrolental cavity central to Weigert's, Cloquet's canal potential space embryogenesis contained hyaloid artery supply developing lens & vitreous disappears by 8 months gestation; Remnants: posterior lens Mittendorf dots, optic disc Bergmeister papillae; Zonules: 1 Preequatorial Canal of Hannover, 2 Post equatorial Canal of Petit, 3 Hyaloid zonules Weigert's ligament; Equator active mitosis E cells columnar dividing elongating to new lens fibres; A cells anterior epithelial metabolically active; Thickness 21 μm anterior pre-equatorial, 17 μm equator, 23 μm posterior pre-equatorial, 4 μm posterior pole.

units.title: Structure of lens — capsule, nucleus, sutures, matrix
units.guide: Capsule outermost/protective thickest basement membrane in body type IV collagen thinnest posterior pole thickest posterior pre-equatorial zone; Anterior epithelium contains A cells & E cells; Posterior epithelium absent in adults formed primary fibres during embryogenesis; Cortex formed by E cells & posterior epithelium; Nucleus table: Embryonic Day 27 fertilization oldest Primary, Fetal during implantation uterine wall Secondary, Infantile immediately after birth Secondary, Adult 1 month after birth youngest Secondary; Sutures seen in fetal nucleus D/t formation & interdigitations embryonic nucleus Anterior Y Apical processes Posterior λ inverted Y Basal processes; Lens matrix architecture Anterior pole Optical axis Nucleus Curved fibres anterior to posterior Horizontal fibres Hexagonal cross section Axial indentation Radial indentation Lens equator Posterior pole.

units.title: Biochemistry — proteins and antioxidants
units.guide: Sequestered antigen lens protein released from capsule during surgery/trauma; Ascorbic acid transport mediated by SVCT2; Proteins: Water-soluble crystallins α most important heat shock prevents denaturation, β maximum amount, γ, HMWP HM1 HM2; Water insoluble urea soluble Vimentin/Filensin crystal proteins, urea insoluble MIP 26 AKA Aquaporin 0 maintains transparency hydration, HMWP HM3 HM4 ↑ in cataract; Antioxidants Vitamin C, E, Glutathione reductase, Superoxide dismutase, Catalase, Vitreous maintains low O2 Removal ↑ propensity cataract; Note Vitamin A does not act as antioxidant.

units.title: Metabolism — sorbitol pathway and cataract
units.guide: Vitamin A does not act as antioxidant; Tryptophan deficiency ↓ Kynurenine and antioxidants except SOD → ↑ cataract animal model; Metabolism Aqueous 90% glucose Vitreous 10% via simple & facilitated diffusion Lens metabolism >80% Anaerobic glycolysis >15% Kreb's cycle HMP shunt <5% Sorbitol pathway; Hyperglycemia Diabetes Adults Galactosemia Children inhibits anaerobic glycolysis rate limiting feedback inhibition increases sorbitol pathway activity ↑ sorbitol Aldose reductase ↔ fructose Cannot diffuse out → ↑ sugars inside → ↑ osmotic pressure → fluid into lens → opaque/hazy cataract.
